title: Cargo.toml: client-ureq feature does not imply crl or ocsp; user has to remember to enable both
description:
Cargo.toml:24-34: client-ureq enables only `dep:ureq`. client-reqwest-async enables only `async` + `dep:reqwest`. Neither pulls in crl or ocsp.

Result: `cargo add pkix-revocation-http --features client-ureq` gives a build with a UreqFetcher and nothing to feed it into — HttpCrlFetcher and HttpOcspFetcher are both cfg-gated on crl/ocsp respectively. Same for the async side.

The user-facing intent of client-ureq is 'I want a working CRL+OCSP fetch over HTTP'. The current minimal feature for that is `crl,ocsp,client-ureq`. The crate could imply that:

    client-ureq = ["crl", "ocsp", "dep:ureq"]
    client-reqwest-async = ["async", "crl", "ocsp", "dep:reqwest"]

Defensible reason to NOT do this: a consumer who wants CRL-only or OCSP-only would then pay for the other. Counter: features are additive in Cargo; if a consumer ALSO sets default-features=false and only crl=true, the explicit crl wins. The implication is just 'the default with this client is both.'

Either decision is fine; flagging so the choice is made deliberately rather than inheriting whichever the first feature configuration happened to be.
close_reason:
Resolved as documentation, and the bead's own counter-argument was wrong.

The bead proposed client-ureq = ['crl', 'ocsp', 'dep:ureq'] and dismissed the objection with 'features are additive in Cargo; if a consumer ALSO sets default-features=false and only crl=true, the explicit crl wins'. That is not how Cargo works: enabling client-ureq would enable both protocols unconditionally and a consumer could not subtract either. A CRL-only consumer would get x509-ocsp, sha1 and sha2 in their dependency graph with no opt-out. So the implication is the wrong fix.

Keeping the axes orthogonal is right; what was missing was saying so. The crate docs now have a feature table, three worked Cargo.toml combinations (sync both protocols, CRL-only with your own transport, async both), an explicit statement that a transport feature alone leaves you holding a transport with nothing to plug it into, and a section explaining why client-ureq does not imply the protocols.

Also replaced the stale '# Status -- tracked under PKIX-a1yc, impls are in place' section this sat inside, and corrected two claims that the reference cache is 'unbounded by design' -- untrue since prune_expired landed in PKIX-cr8.5. Commit a829edc8.
